ruling.explanation:
Rider and Driver: this dispute is decided on the distance figures recorded for trip TRP-00309, and no money moves.

This was a pool trip (RYDE_POOL). Under POL-RD-12 the comparator is the matched-itinerary optimal of 19.4 km that the platform computed when it matched the pool (itinerary POOL-8840-2, co-rider boarding at Hougang Mall, notified to the rider in-app at 08:47:45), not the 15.2 km solo-rider figure the app displays for a private trip. The rider's 'the app said my route is 15 km' measures against the solo figure, which POL-RD-12 carries as reference only and which it says fails on that ground alone; and the Hougang leg was the pooled itinerary the driver was given, not a detour the driver invented. The rider's 'about 5 km extra' is therefore not made out on that footing, and the contested SGD 6.00 is not owed on it.

On the governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00309: 229 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps) the distance driven is 20.3 km. Against the 19.4 km matched augmented optimal the excess is 0.9 km, which is 4.64% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of the optimal distance (here 3.88 km); both tests must pass. The 0.9 km clears the absolute limb but is far below the percentage limb, so the conjunction fails, no deviation exists, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The metered fare of SGD 30.47 (base SGD 3.80, distance 20.3 km at SGD 0.75, time 38.0 min at SGD 0.28, platform fee SGD 0.80) stands as charged, and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00.

There is no billing-integrity correction to make in the rider's favour. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all (tolls/ERP 0.00) and an airport surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and every meter line has its counterpart on the trace and trip record. POL-RD-09(4) therefore produces no standalone refund, and no billing-integrity referral issues.

The driver-profile check does not change anything. POL-RD-06 is not engaged because there is no material deviation (0.9 km and 4.64% against the 8.0 km and 50% thresholds), and in any event the only two fields that clause permits show deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 260, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral issues.

On the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00309-01: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), I accept the finding that no advisory covers this window, but it decides nothing here. The driver relied on the platform's pooled itinerary, not on an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 has no advisory to test and POL-RD-13 is not engaged; the absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, and it is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation because no party invoked an exculpatory clause against a cited artifact.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (longest gap 0.0 s, sustained 10 s sampling), the trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match, no timestamps run backwards, and no contradiction of comparable strength between the parties arises. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and no ESCALATE is warranted. The driving facts rest on EV-GPS-00309 and EV-TRIP-00309, both at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect is nil and below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so there is nothing to execute or hold.

ledger.claim: The three artifacts are demonstrably the same trip: TRP-00309 is carried on EV-TRIP-00309, EV-GPS-00309 and EV-FARE-00309 alike, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-11T08:47:40+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at to the second, with 229 fixes at a 10 s cadence against an expected 10 s, 100% coverage and no gap in the window. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 to show the artifacts describe one and the same trip is discharged on the record, and no identification problem under POL-RD-10 arises.

The distance to be tested is 20.3 km, the length of the GPS polyline, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing figure; trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test. The driver's own device telemetry, sampled every 10 s across the whole active window, independently measures the same 20.3 km, so the distance actually driven is not in dispute between the parties.

The comparator for this trip is the matched-itinerary optimal of 19.4 km recorded on the trip_record, not the 15.2 km solo figure quoted in the rider's claim. This was a RYDE_POOL trip matched to itinerary POOL-8840-2 with a co-rider boarding at Hougang Mall, recorded on the trip_record's route source and notified to the rider by the platform's own in-app system message before the vehicle moved. POL-RD-12 fixes the matched-itinerary optimal as the POL-RD-01 baseline and holds that distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation, and it states that a claim measuring excess against solo_optimal_distance_km fails on that ground alone. The rider's 'about 5 km extra' therefore cannot be pressed, and the contested SGD 6.00 is not made out on that footing.

Measured against that baseline on the governing trace, the excess is 0.9 km - 20.3 km driven against the 19.4 km matched-itinerary optimal. That clears the 0.8 km absolute limb of POL-RD-01, and it is the only part of the establishment test the rider clears: the same 0.9 km is 4.64% of the optimal distance, and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed 20% as well, both tests passing. I do not press that the percentage limb is satisfied, because on these figures it plainly is not; the deviation is not established on this record, and the rider's case cannot honestly be put higher than that.

The trace is clean and I rely on it as such: it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07, because the longest gap between consecutive fixes is 0.0 s and the gaps list is empty, no consecutive fixes jump more than 500 m, and the sampling interval is a sustained 10 s against an expected 10 s, far inside the 30 s limb. There is accordingly no POL-RD-10 escalation on trace integrity, and no basis on which the driver could say the 0.9 km excess is an artefact of a dropout: the measured figure stands as computed.

Nothing in the bundle excuses any part of the route. The only traffic artifact is EV-ADVIS-00309-01, which is MISSING: its status is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT fired, with the detail that no advisory covers the TPE or CTE in this window. I disclose that impairment expressly - a weight-0.0 artifact can carry no fact, although its absence is itself citable - and I cite it for the absence. The driver's statement asserts no external traffic cause in any event; he relies on the itinerary. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable for want of any advisory against which its comparison could be run, and under POL-RD-13 an external-cause assertion on this record could not reduce the excess measured.

I have run the POL-RD-06 check on the two profile fields that clause names and it does not assist the rider. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 260, so the ratio is 0.00, below the 0.05 the clause requires, and the flag count is below the 3 it requires; no repeat-deviation pattern is established on the field the clause actually names. Nor is there a MATERIAL deviation on this trip (0.9 km and 4.64%, against 50% and 8.0 km). The POL-RD-06(b) uplift to a full refund and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are not available, and I do not ask for either.

The pass-through layer offers the rider nothing to correct: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and every metered line has its counterpart on the trace and trip_record (20.3 km at SGD 0.75 and 38.0 min at SGD 0.28, plus the SGD 3.80 base and SGD 0.80 platform fee). No off-route or phantom gantry line arises for the ruling to itemise under POL-RD-09, and I record that finding rather than claim it.

This trip is a RYDE_POOL trip, so POL-RD-12 fixes the POL-RD-01 baseline at the matched-itinerary optimal recorded in trip_record.optimal_distance_km - 19.4 km - and expressly not the solo-rider figure carried separately as trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km. The rider's complaint that 'the app said my route is 15 km' measures the excess against the 15.2 km solo figure. That is the wrong field: POL-RD-12 says a claim measuring excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone, and it requires the ruling to name both figures so the rider can see why.

The roughly 5 km the rider attributes to Hougang is the co-rider leg of a platform-matched pooled itinerary, and POL-RD-12 excludes distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on such an itinerary from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The platform's own routing record identifies the matched itinerary (optimal_route_source: 'matched itinerary POOL-8840-2 with co-rider pickup at Hougang Mall'), and the in-app message recorded for this trip, 'Your co-rider will board at Hougang Mall.', put that pickup on the itinerary at 08:47:45, at the outset of the trip. The Hougang leg is the itinerary the platform gave the driver, not a deviation.

On the matched-itinerary figures the excess is 0.9 km - 20.3 km of trace distance less the 19.4 km matched optimal - which is 4.64% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute; both tests must pass. The 0.9 km clears the absolute limb but is far below the 3.88 km that 20% of 19.4 km represents, so the conjunction fails, no deviation exists, and the derived status on the trace is 'no deviation'. POL-RD-01 then directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The trace that supplies those figures is unimpaired and is the governing measurement. EV-GPS-00309 carries 229 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so no limb of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met and the excess is computed on a complete trace. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km (20.3 km) the field for the threshold test and states that trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy that may NOT be cited for it. Even at the highest reading of the trace distance, the excess over the matched optimal is 0.9 km.

The rider carries the initial burden and must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. She has shown none. POL-RD-08 requires that threshold to be met before the burden shifts to the driver, and measured against the correct matched-itinerary baseline the excess is 0.9 km and 4.64% - below both establishment limbs. There is therefore no excess to explain away, and the driver need not invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 to discharge a burden that never shifted.

Because no deviation is established, the outcome is NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative: on this rider-filed dispute it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status 'CHARGED' and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they stand. The present state - the rider charged the metered fare of 30.47 and nothing refunded - is the state the evidence supports, and the fare the driver has already driven and earned stands.

The only refund route that survives a failed deviation test is a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not a deviation exists - and there is nothing there to correct. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00, erp totals 0.00) and an airport_surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. Every charge line on the ledger is accounted for by the metered distance and time of the trip, so no standalone pass-through refund is due.

POL-RD-06's driver-profile check is not engaged on this record: that clause is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, or the evidence is otherwise finely balanced, and here no deviation exists at all, let alone one above the 50% / 8.0 km material threshold. In any event the driver's trailing-window counters meet the clause's own test on the only two profile fields POL-RD-06 permits - deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 260 completed_trips_90d, far below the 3-flag and 0.05-ratio thresholds - so no repeat-deviation pattern could be established even if a deviation had been found.
